title: Everest: Just go for it
author: Randall Posey

quotes.q: We were on the mountain for 35 days. It was an incredible experience, and definitely [a] lived dream.
quotes.sum: UNL alum Griffin Mims is describing his Everest expedition, which lasted 35 days and which he calls a dream come true.

quotes.q: There were less than 200 on the north side.
quotes.sum: UNL alum Griffin Mims is describing how few climbers were on the north side of Mount Everest when he reached the summit. He stood on top almost alone with his expedition team for nearly an hour.

title: Cornelius turns up for his first birthday
author: Colton Knott

quotes.q: It’s a little bit goofy; we’re aware of that.
quotes.sum: A UNL communications specialist is explaining why the university threw a cake-and-candles birthday party for Cornelius, its student-texting AI chatbot, on the day it turned one.

quotes.q: They don’t have to carve out time to send text messages.
quotes.sum: A UNL communications specialist is describing a benefit of the Cornelius chatbot: it handles routine text messages to students, so advisors can spend their time on more meaningful one-on-one work.

title: Charmed by Chels owner talks being a student entrepreneur, future plans
author: Brooklynn Pierce

quotes.q: I got to turn the hobby into an actual business, which has been so awesome, getting to do something that I just love to do, and getting to make a business out of it.
quotes.sum: Chelsea Mahloch, a full-time UNL student, is reflecting on how her hobby of making charm jewelry became her business, Charmed by Chels.

quotes.q: It's definitely not a perfect science, but I'm working towards it every day.
quotes.sum: Chelsea Mahloch, a full-time UNL student, is describing how she balances running her jewelry business with being a full-time student.

title: Mike Flood wins race for Nebraska’s 1st Congressional District
author: Colton Knott, Paige Nickless

quotes.q: I am so proud of the movement we built, proud of the campaign we ran and proud that we focused on the issues that mattered to Nebraskans.
quotes.sum: Democrat Chris Backemeyer is reflecting on his campaign after conceding the 1st Congressional District race to Republican Rep. Mike Flood.

quotes.q: Together, we motivated thousands of Nebraskans to make their voices heard, hold our government accountable, and send a message that the status quo isn’t good enough.
quotes.sum: Democrat Chris Backemeyer's closing message in his concession statement after losing the 1st Congressional District race to Rep. Mike Flood.

title: Celebrate 45 years of friendship with the Ross
author: Jaxson Beck

quotes.q: We love working with them and we hope that students will enjoy the films.
quotes.sum: UNL's Mary Riepma Ross Media Arts Center is showing a series of films from 1981 to celebrate 45 years of its support group, Friends of the Ross. Its programming director is explaining the choice.

quotes.q: We really had a kind of urgent mission to raise money and to grow the audience, which is still our mission, but it’s not quite as urgent.
quotes.sum: Someone connected to the Ross Media Arts Center is looking back at the early days of its support group, Friends of the Ross, founded in 1981 to raise money and build an audience.

title: Nebraska football’s special teams search for consistency as kicking woes persist
author: Matthew Malloy

quotes.q: It's hard to win a game when you miss these crucial field goals.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is talking about the team's kicking problems after another late-game loss, and who is responsible for the missed field goals.

quotes.q: Obviously that’s the kicker. It’s also the snapper putting the ball in the [holder’s] hands. We have to be better in that area.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is spreading the blame for Nebraska's missed field goals beyond the kicker to the snapper and the holder.

title: RODRIGUEZ: November must look different for Nebraska football than prior years
author: Eli Rodriguez

quotes.q: Water’s rocky and the ocean’s rocky; it’s just steady in the boat.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is answering questions about Nebraska's third straight fourth-quarter collapse. He says the team should stay steady rather than make a rough stretch worse.

quotes.q: Don’t take a rocking boat and a rocking sea, and rock it even more.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is using a boat metaphor to explain how he wants Nebraska to respond to its three-game losing streak.

title: Denise Powell takes House seat for Nebraska’s 2nd Congressional District
author: Natalie Hill, Justin Diep

quotes.q: I am sorry I couldn’t lead the team to a better result.
quotes.sum: Republican Brinker Harding is speaking at his Omaha watch party after losing the 2nd Congressional District race to Democrat Denise Powell.

title: Midterm Live Updates: Jim Pillen secures victory in Nebraska governor’s race
author: Daily Nebraskan Staff

quotes.q: You chose a leader, not a politician, and I will never forget that trust.
quotes.sum: Gov. Jim Pillen is thanking voters at his election-night watch party after the AP called the governor's race for him.

author: Paige Nickless

quotes.q: We're trying to determine who it was and then determine whether they'll both be cited for disturbing the peace by fighting.
quotes.sum: UNL's interim police chief is explaining the investigation into a fight in an Abel Hall hallway on Halloween night.

quotes.q: So, basically, you're not allowed to sell unless you have a trademark infringement type of situation.
quotes.sum: UNL's interim police chief is describing the rules for selling goods on or near campus, after police dealt with someone doing so over Halloween weekend.

title: Nebraska football looks to respond to sour loss on short week
author: Alex Berry

quotes.q: Today’s a Tuesday practice; we had a Monday practice last night.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is explaining that Nebraska's schedule is shifted forward a day to prepare for a Friday night game at Illinois, after a fourth-quarter loss to Washington.

quotes.q: It’s going to be right to that game.
quotes.sum: A Nebraska defensive lineman is talking about turning the page to Friday's game at Illinois after the 17-10 loss to Washington.

title: UNL students share opinions on online sports betting initiatives
author: Isabel Hoiberg

quotes.q: I don’t think they should be pressuring 18-year-old athletes, and some players even get death threats.
quotes.sum: A UNL student is explaining why they're wary of legalized sports betting in Nebraska, one of the ballot initiatives voters decided in the midterm election.

title: Nebraska men’s basketball fishes out Le Moyne after slow start in season opener
author: Danny Berg

quotes.q: I thought we traded baskets a little bit with them early and at the beginning of the second half.
quotes.sum: Nebraska men's basketball coach Fred Hoiberg is assessing the season-opening 106-64 win over Le Moyne, where the Huskers started slowly before pulling away.

quotes.q: Other than that, our movement was terrific. We executed the game plan of not driving into a crowd.
quotes.sum: Nebraska men's basketball coach Fred Hoiberg is praising Nebraska's ball movement and game plan after its season-opening blowout of Le Moyne.

title: Takeaways from Nebraska women’s basketball’s win over San Jose State
author: Connor Krumme

quotes.q: That’s going to be really important… I just want to get to the point where rebounding is the first thing that comes to our mind.
quotes.sum: Nebraska women's basketball coach Amy Williams is talking about rebounding after Nebraska out-rebounded San Jose State in its season-opening win.

quotes.q: If you can go get offensive rebounds the way we have, then that makes up for a lot.
quotes.sum: Nebraska women's basketball coach Amy Williams is explaining why rebounding matters. She says the Huskers' offensive rebounds made up for a lot in their season-opening win over San Jose State.

title: Rhule rundown: Washington recap, scouting Illinois
author: Alex Berry, Eli Rodriguez

quotes.q: I love Jacory Barney. You couldn’t get me to turn on him in a million years, man.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is defending receiver Jacory Barney Jr., who played through a broken rib against Washington.

quotes.q: I would step in front of a train for him.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is expressing how fiercely he stands behind Jacory Barney Jr., who played all four quarters with a broken rib.

title: University of Nebraska-Lincoln to open off-campus library
author: Noora Mohamed

quotes.q: They're bringing into proximity some different collections and services that could have some really cool synergies among them.
quotes.sum: A UNL libraries leader is describing the second floor of the new downtown central library, where the university's library collections and services will sit alongside the city library's.

quotes.q: If they need access to the libraries in some way, and that building is closer to wherever it is that they live downtown.
quotes.sum: A UNL librarian is explaining who benefits from the university's first off-campus library: students who live downtown and find it closer than the main campus libraries.

title: RODRIGUEZ: Nebraska football is in a dangerous position after loss to Washington
author: Eli Rodriguez

quotes.q: We have to find a way to get more offensive production, score more points to win these games.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is reacting to Nebraska's 17-10 loss to Washington, its third straight loss decided late in the game.

quotes.q: Three turnovers and a missed field goal are not a recipe to win.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is explaining why Nebraska lost to Washington 17-10.

title: Takeaways from Nebraska football’s loss to Washington
author: Alex Berry

quotes.q: I certainly understand how frustrated everyone is that this has happened three games in a row.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is responding to fan frustration after Nebraska's third straight fourth-quarter collapse, a 17-10 loss to Washington.

quotes.q: But all I can do is show up tomorrow and get back to work for Illinois.
quotes.sum: Nebraska football coach Matt Rhule is looking ahead to the Illinois game after the Washington loss, saying all he can do is get back to work.

title: Bus, bikes, skates: UNL students look to alternatives from cars
author: Chloe Fitzgibbon

quotes.q: It's gonna take longer to get there if I bike than if I drive usually, but if I bike and I get some exercise in, I also get some fresh air.
quotes.sum: A UNL sophomore who bikes everywhere is describing the tradeoffs of biking over driving to get around Lincoln.

quotes.q: With the prices being what they are, I’d rather not have to drop 80 bucks every month, so I tend to try to stick on campus for the most part.
quotes.sum: A UNL sophomore is explaining why he mostly sticks to campus and a bike instead of driving: he doesn't want to spend about $80 a month on gas.

title: Phi Delt supports brother with ‘Nightmare on R Street’
author: Maliya Keeshan

quotes.q: Someone mentioned the idea and instantly from there we tried to make it happen.
quotes.sum: The Phi Delt chapter president is describing how the fraternity quickly decided to take on its cause this year through its haunted house.

quotes.q: It’s a core memory, we even have some sophomores and juniors back volunteering.
quotes.sum: A Phi Delta Theta member is describing what the fraternity's annual haunted house means to the chapter, including older members who come back to volunteer.

title: PRESS PLAY: High-octane ‘Car Bar’ intoxicates the Daily Nebraskan office
author: Jalen-Thomas Kroger

quotes.q: I immediately hopped on, and immediately clicked with everybody.
quotes.sum: Car Bar guitarist Holden Stoner is recalling how he joined the band after being recruited to add more sound, and how quickly he clicked with the members.

quotes.q: I was like, ‘Screw it, why not,’.
quotes.sum: Car Bar drummer Conor Macguire is explaining why he said yes when the band invited him to jam during his final year of college.
